ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertices of the quadrilateral are arranged in the order W-X-Z-Y, and the shape is a rhombus; W is at the upper left, X is at the upper right, Z is at the lower right, and Y is at the lower left. The diagonals WZ and XY are drawn in the figure, and they intersect at point T. The required ∠YWZ is the angle at vertex W formed by side WY and diagonal WZ. Reasoning: The problem gives that WXZY is a rhombus, and m∠XZY = 56°, which is the interior angle at vertex Z. The opposite angles of a rhombus are equal, so the interior angle ∠YWX at vertex W is also equal to 56°. The diagonals of a rhombus bisect the angles at their endpoints, so diagonal WZ bisects ∠YWX. Thus m∠YWZ = 56° ÷ 2 = 28°.

raw_record.question_text: Quadrilateral $WXZY$ is a rhombus. If $m\angle XZY=56$, find $m\angle YWZ$.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the rhombus vertices in order W-X-Z-Y, with diagonal WZ drawn from W to Z; the requested angle YWZ is the angle at W between side WY and diagonal WZ. From the text, use that WXZY is a rhombus and that m∠XZY, the interior angle at Z, is 56°. In a rhombus, opposite angles are congruent, so the interior angle at W is also 56°. Also, each diagonal of a rhombus bisects the angles at its endpoints; therefore diagonal WZ bisects ∠YWX. Thus m∠YWZ = 56° / 2 = 28°.

method.method_draft: From the image, focus on triangle WYZ formed by side WY, side YZ, and diagonal WZ; the desired angle YWZ is one base angle of this triangle. From the text, know WXZY is a rhombus, so all sides are equal, giving WY = YZ. Also m∠XZY = 56° is the interior angle at Z of the rhombus. Since adjacent angles in a rhombus are supplementary, the interior angle at Y is m∠WYZ = 180° - 56° = 124°. In triangle WYZ, sides WY and YZ are equal, so it is isosceles and its base angles at W and Z are equal. Therefore each base angle is (180° - 124°) / 2 = 28°, so m∠YWZ = 28°.
